plan.title: bug(harness): host agent memory must not override Directive process SoT without USER.md consent

narratives.Description: bug(harness): host agent memory must not override Directive process SoT without USER.md consent
narratives.Overview:
1. **Authority class (P2).** Name host agent memory (Grok memory-v2 / Cursor memory / Claude memory / equivalent host stores) as **external context** in the same sentence family as Warp Drive / MCP / prompt-injected. USER.md `"Personal (always wins)"` remains the only Personal override SoT. ⊗ Treat host-memory preference topics as USER.md. ⊗ Invent a second Personal SoT.

2. **Mandatory consumer land (F1).** The host-memory class MUST land in `content/templates/agents-entry.md` Session routing (and refresh via `#1309` `agents:refresh`). Maintainer `AGENTS.md` alone does not relieve P2 for consumer deposits. Also pointer in inter-run-learning docs (item 5).

3. **Conflict rule + lock (P1 / F2 / F6).** When host memory (or other external context) contradicts a closed skill/contract field, follow the contract/skill. Require a one-line durable conflict disclosure (main-chat or Stop 1 / parent recording line naming that host memory was discarded for that field). Ship a closed conflict example: design-critique Dual-stop spend front door (`spend-recommend` → `spend-ask: resolved` on bare arc) wins over a host-memory "always ask" note — locked by content-contract string and/or `evaluateSpendRecord` / authority fixture (extend existing spend fixtures; do not leave Prefer-A as prose-only).

4. **Read-time unsigned rule (F3).** Preference/process-shaped host-memory notes without `operator-asked` (or equivalent explicit operator-confirm provenance) have **zero Personal authority** even when they do not token-collide with a named closed field. They may inform rediscovery facts; they must not invent process obligations (e.g. "bare arc must ask") that change front doors already closed by contract. Write-consent (ask-to-save / confirm + provenance tags) remains for *new* preference-class writes; it does not replace this read rule for notes already on disk.

5. **Inter-run inventory exclusion (F4).** Add host agent-memory products as an explicit **non-SoT / external-context exclusion** in inter-run-learning §3 (or adjacent) so #2741/#2742 readers do not treat them as an unlisted Directive memory SoT. Cite analysis §4.1 / §4.4 (operator-gated USER.md edits; agent-written untrusted vs operator USER.md) as carry-forward — do not invent a parallel trust story.

6. **Promotion path + consumer freedom (F5).** Wanted local process deltas go to USER.md Personal (or `decision:write` + issue when framework-bound). Optional "promote this memory line into USER.md?" only on explicit operator confirm. Framework does **not** ban a consented Personal "always ask on bare arc"; it bans *unsigned* host memory from acting as that override.

7. **Non-goals (v1 hold).** No rewriting Grok/Cursor/Claude memory products inside Directive; no delete-all host memory; no auto-sync of host memory into USER.md.

8. **Acceptance.**
   - agents-entry Session routing carries host-memory ∈ external context + Personal-only override sentence; `agents:refresh` path noted
   - inter-run-learning exclusion row landed
   - Closed conflict fixture/DCR: host-memory "always ask" loses to spend-recommend resolve; one-line conflict disclosure required when closed field wins
   - Unsigned/unprovenanced preference notes → non-Personal (fixture or content-contract lock)
   - No second Personal SoT beside USER.md

design-critique: warranted, because host-side agent memory (e.g. Grok memory-v2 preference topics) can silently override live Directive skill/contract closed forms without USER.md Personal consent, treating unsigned host notes as Personal authority.

Dual-stop cap: 6 posts

pain: P1, P2

- P1. Unauthorized process override: host agent-memory preference/process notes can beat current Directive skill/contract closed forms (e.g. design-critique spend front door) with no USER.md Personal write and no operator confirm.
- P2. Missing authority classification: Agents.md / session routing name USER.md Personal over Warp Drive/MCP/prompt-injected but do not name host agent-memory stores, so agents treat curated host preference topics as Personal; consumers who want local deltas already have USER.md, while unsigned memory bypasses that gate.

## Findings (Prefer-A vs Stop 1 P1/P2)

Pin: `0f97a84c8d80a643f34e9bdc2e921c3bfe8a754d`. Read Stop 1 `5980923269` + issue body only. No Bound lean.

### F1 — P2 classification gap is real; Prefer-A names it, but landing surface is underspecified

Pin `AGENTS.md` Returning Sessions carries the only closed external-context sentence: USER.md `"Personal (always wins)"` overrides external context `(Warp Drive / MCP / prompt-injected)`. Host agent-memory stores are absent from that list — matches Stop 1 P2.

Pin `content/templates/agents-entry.md` `## Session routing (#2176)` loads USER.md and confirms alignment, and has **zero** matches for `external context` / `Warp Drive` / `prompt-injected`. Prefer-A acceptance says "agents-entry / session-routing / inter-run-learning pointer". If the host-memory class lands only on maintainer `AGENTS.md` Returning Sessions and skips `content/templates/agents-entry.md` (+ `#1309` `agents:refresh`), consumer deposits keep the P2 silence. Prefer-A does not bind which of those three pointers must carry the new host-memory name, or that agents-entry is mandatory for consumer relief.

### F2 — P1 conflict rule needs a lock surface Prefer-A does not bind

Pin Spend SoT already resolves the #5318 front-door case without host memory:

- `content/contracts/design-critique.md` `### Spend (#4705)`: bare arc with recorded `spend-recommend:` → Stop 1 `spend-ask: resolved`; explicit `n=` overrides.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-design-critique/SKILL.md`: `Spend: closed n= or spend-recommend; else ask.`
- `packages/core/src/design-critique/spend.test.ts` + `design_critique_contract.test.ts` lock `evaluateSpendRecord` / spend-recommend parse.

Prefer-A item 2 ("when host memory contradicts a closed contract/skill field, follow the contract and surface once") is the right P1 relief direction. Acceptance draft wants a "Closed conflict example (design-critique spend front door or equivalent)". Prefer-A sketch does not bind where that example lives (content-contract string pin vs `evaluateSpendRecord` fixture vs DCR authority sentence). Existing spend fixtures lock recommend-resolve; they do **not** encode a host-memory-vs-contract conflict. Without that lock, Prefer-A stays prose and P1 can recur as agent behavior outside the fixture bag.

### F3 — Prefer-A write-consent (item 4) does not cover read-time unsigned notes already on disk

The #5318 trigger (issue body / Stop 1 related) was **following** an existing Grok `topics/preferences.md` bare-arc ask line, not minting a new write. Prefer-A item 4 (write only on ask-to-save/confirm; tag `operator-asked` vs `agent-inferred`) helps future preference writes and does not relieve read-time authority of unsigned notes already present.

Item 1 says host memory "must not invent Personal process prefs" and must not be treated as USER.md. That is directionally correct for P1, but underspecifies the read rule for an on-disk preference-shaped note that lacks provenance: does absence of `operator-asked` mean zero Personal authority even when the note does not literally contradict a named closed field? Conflict rule (item 2) covers contradiction; the #5318 path was inventing an ask obligation that the contract already closed via spend-recommend. Prefer-A needs an explicit unsigned/unprovenanced → non-Personal read rule, or P1 residual remains for "helpful" process notes that do not collide token-for-token with a field name.

Non-goals (no delete-all host memory; no auto-sync into USER.md) are fine and do not block that read-time distrust rule.

### F4 — inter-run-learning pointer underspecifies inventory shape (P2)

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

Host-side agent memory (e.g. Grok Build memory-v2 topic notes under `~/.grok/memory-v2/...`) can silently override live Directive skill/contract closed forms. Agents treat curated host "preferences" as Personal authority without operator consent. That is a consent and SoT bug: only `USER.md` Personal (always wins) is the authorized personal override channel.

Observed on deftai/directive design-critique arc #5318 (2026-10-04): contract/skill say Dual-stop spend is `closed n=` **or** recorded `spend-recommend` (else ask). A Grok workspace memory note said bare `arc N` must ask before Stop 1. Parent asked anyway despite `spend-recommend: N=1`, then stamped `spend-ask: asked` after operator `n=1`. Same spend landed; front door was wrong. Operator never authorized that memory line.

## Pain

- Unauthorized host-memory process overrides beat current Directive SoT with no USER.md write and no confirm.
- Operator (and consumers) cannot tell whether a "preference" was consented or agent-inferred.
- Consumers who *do* want local process deltas already have `USER.md` Personal; host memory minting those deltas bypasses that gate.
- Inter-run learning (#2741 / #2742) inventories Directive SoTs but does not classify host memory products in the authority stack.

## Root cause

Authority stack names `USER.md` Personal over external context (Warp Drive / MCP / prompt-injected) but does **not** name host agent-memory stores. In practice host memory is injected and followed as if it were Personal.

## Prefer-A / Bound note (discussion sketch — not yet arced)

1. Classify host agent memory as **external context** (same class as Warp Drive / MCP / prompt-injected): may inform; must not override closed skill/contract forms; must not invent Personal process prefs. ⊗ Treat host-memory preference topics as USER.md.
2. Conflict rule: when host memory contradicts a closed contract/skill field, follow the contract and surface once.
3. Promotion path: wanted local process deltas go to `USER.md` Personal (or `decision:write` + issue when framework-bound); optional "promote this line into USER.md?" only on explicit confirm.
4. Write consent for preference-class host memory: only on operator ask-to-save or confirm; tag provenance (`operator-asked` vs `agent-inferred`) so inferred overrides are distrustable.
5. Keep consumer freedom: Personal overrides stay legal via USER.md. Framework does not ban "always ask on bare arc"; it bans *unsigned* host memory from acting as that override.

Non-goals v1: rewriting Grok/Cursor/Claude memory products inside Directive; deleting all host memory; auto-syncing memory into USER.md.

## Acceptance (draft)

- [ ] agents-entry / session-routing / inter-run-learning pointer: host agent memory is external context; process overrides require USER.md Personal or explicit operator confirm
- [ ] Closed conflict example (design-critique spend front door or equivalent fixture): host-memory "always ask" loses to contract `spend-recommend` resolve path
- [ ] DCR or content-contract lock for the authority sentence(s)
- [ ] No second competing Personal SoT invented beside USER.md

## Repro (this workspace)

1. Bare operator cue `arc 5318` with no `n=` token.
2. Parent records `spend-recommend: N=1` then still asks Dual-stop spend because Grok `topics/preferences.md` says bare arc asks before Stop 1.
3. Live skill line: "Spend: closed n= or spend-recommend; else ask." Contract #4705: bare arc with recommend → `spend-ask: resolved`.

## Refs

- Skill: `content/skills/deft-directive-design-critique/SKILL.md` Spend pointer
- Contract: `content/contracts/design-critique.md` § Spend (#4705)
- USER.md Personal always-wins / external context: Agents.md session routing
- Inter-run learning SoTs: #2741 / #2742 / `content/docs/inter-run-learning.md`
- Trigger arc: #5318
